key_insight: The paper introduces "frame width" as a new code design metric—the smallest logical-operator weight cutoff that still allows a complete canonical basis—showing that low-weight, full regular logical bases are sometimes fundamentally obstructed even when distance is high.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum computing, the results help quantify and reduce logical-operator overhead, improving resource estimation, logical gate compilation, and practical code selection beyond distance alone.
method: Define group-valued codes with translated seed operators to generate full regular canonical logical bases.
Analyze structural obstructions and sufficient conditions for regularity in CSS codes over different group orders.
Demonstrate the framework on high-rate lifted-product and pair-partition codes, plus symmetry-reduction/stabilizer-pruning for exact distance certification.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit large-code examples—an [[1088,128,22]] LP code with f=22 and an [[1024,256,24]] PP code with f<=27, including a proved-optimal f=25 case at w=11, and exact distance certification for LP codes with more than 1,000 qubits.
watch_item: Frame width depends on the existence of a complete canonical basis, so codes with favorable distance may still require heavier logical operators or fail regularity under certain group/check-matrix structures.
paper_title: Designing Group-Valued Codes with Full Regular Low-Weight Bases
